title: add-traffic-temperature-escrow-canary-and-probe-tempering
author: Anjali Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Canary evaluators are highly sensitive to short-lived traffic bursts and transient client-side retry behavior. This leads to noisy rollbacks or unnecessary escalation in canary-driven rollouts. The change introduces a traffic 'temperature' abstraction plus an escrowed probe credit system and probe-tempering scheduler that (1) smooths probe injection rates across traffic modalities, (2) biases probe selection away from high-variance slices during short bursts, and (3) holds a small reserve of 'escrow' probe credit to perform decisive probes when signal quality improves.

Design summary: We add a traffic_temperature metric derived from short-term burstiness (variance / mean over 1m/5m windows), request size distribution, and concurrency spikes. A probe_tempo scheduler consumes a per-slice budget and adjusts probe pacing using a leaky-bucket softened by an adaptive sigma scale. Probe escrows are minted when temperature is low and consumed when we need higher confidence (e.g., before automatic rollback). When temperature is high, the scheduler reduces probe aggressiveness and increases the confidence window. The canary evaluator integrates temperature and escrow signals to compute a tempered regression score that replaces a hard delta threshold with a probabilistic gating function.

Implementation notes: Changes touch the canary evaluator (go/perf/canary/evaluator.go), the probe scheduler (go/perf/canary/scheduler.go), telemetry mapping (telemetry/metrics.yaml), and the operator config (deploy/helm/values-canary.yaml). New configuration knobs: canary.temperature.window_seconds, canary.temperature.sigma_smoothing, canary.escrow.initial_credits, and canary.scheduler.max_probe_qps. Defaults are conservative. The core algorithm is implemented in evaluator.go with extensive unit tests covering extreme burst and steady-state cases.

Testing: Unit tests (pkg/perf/canary/*_test.go) cover synthetic burst traces, skewed request-size distributions and coordinated concurrency spikes. We added an integration job in CI that runs a canary simulation harness (ci/canary-sim) that exercises the escrow behavior under a deterministic pseudo-random workload generator. Local load tests on staging were run for 48h with both steady and bursty traffic shapes; we observed a 45% reduction in false-positive rollback triggers and maintained sensitivity to real regressions.

Observability and rollout: New metrics exposed: canary.traffic_temperature, canary.escrow_balance, canary.temper_regression_score. Dashboards were added under observability/dashboards/canary-temperature.json. Default rollout is a staged deploy: enable in canary mode for a single zone, monitor two full canaries (1% and 5%) for a day, then global enable. We included an automatic opt-out flag: canary.enable_temperature = false to revert to legacy behavior.

Backward compatibility: The change is backward-compatible with existing canary configs; if temperature is disabled, behavior is unchanged. The escrow system is internal to the evaluator and does not require customer-facing schema changes.

Risks and mitigations: Miscalibration of temperature thresholds could under-detect regressions during coordinated traffic shifts. To mitigate, initial defaults are conservative and the rollout plan includes manual gates and additional alerting (see release_notes).

Related: ENG-2769 implements additional canary telemetry; SUP-1123 was the incident that motivated this work.

Checklist: - [x] Design review with SRE and Core Runtime - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] CI passes on first attempt with one flaky test re-run - [x] Docs/observability dashboards included - [x] Rollout plan in PR description

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Good direction. Two requests: (1) show a small worked example of temperature values for a typical burst and (2) make the escrow initial_credits configurable by release channel.
Author (Anjali Kapoor): Added example table to docs/runbooks/canary-temperature.md and made initial_credits pluggable in helm values. PTAL.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look comprehensive. One nit: the scheduler's random jitter is not seeded in the deterministic integration job, causing flakiness. Recommend deterministic seed for CI.
Author (Anjali Kapoor): Seed fixed in ci/jobs/canary-sim.yaml; re-ran CI and flakes are gone.
Hector Ruiz: Observability looks good; please add an alert for escrow_balance<10% during an active canary so SRE gets notified before auto-rollbacks occur.
Author (Anjali Kapoor): Added alert rule canary_escrow_low (prometheus rule) and documented escalation path in runbook.
release_notes: Adds traffic_temperature and escrowed probe scheduling to the canary evaluator to reduce false-positive rollbacks during short lived bursts. Exposes canary.traffic_temperature, canary.escrow_balance, and canary.temper_regression_score metrics. Default behavior is conservative and offload is opt-out via canary.enable_temperature=false. See docs/runbooks/canary-temperature.md for calibration guidance.
notes_for_backport: Backport to release/2026-Q1 if customers on Dedicated report increased rollback noise; ensure helm values are also backported.
manual_steps_after_merge: 1) Update monitoring dashboards in Grafana using observability/dashboards/canary-temperature.json. 2) Schedule a canary-traffic test for 24h in staging and run ENG-2769 validation. 3) Notify SRE on-call for first six rollouts.
estimated_impact: Reduction in false-positive canary rollbacks by ~45% on staging workloads; small CPU overhead (~2%) on evaluator path.
qa_summary: Unit tests and a deterministic integration sim guard behavior under controlled bursts. Staging 48h soak with bursty traffic showed expected throttling of probe injection and preserved detection for synthetic regressions.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): add traffic temperature and escrowed probe scheduler to reduce noisy rollbacks
